sources.default_view: Camera the results playback opens on. down_the_line looks along the target line from behind the golfer; once the run's address ball and feet are known the camera sits on the line midway between them (behind_fraction in native_viewer_export/camera_framing_settings.json), as the owner asked on 2026-11-22. Any VIEW_ORDER preset is allowed.
sources.render_stretch: Share of the playback panel's height given to the 3D render; the plot below gets plot_stretch. 5:2 leaves the render about 70% (owner asked on 2026-11-22 that the swing, not the plot, fill the window).
sources.plot_stretch: Share of the playback panel's height given to the time-series plot (see render_stretch).
sources.hide_editor_docks: While the Results Playback tab is on top, hide the Model Segments and Properties docks so the swing gets the window; the 3D Viewport tab (or View menu) brings them back.
sources.slider_min_width_px: Narrowest the timeline slider may get; the transport row (Play, slider, View, Speed, Export) stays on one row and the window's minimum width grows instead of the slider collapsing to its handle.
sources.camera_distance_m: Camera distance in metres per view; only the views listed override the shared preset's default_distance_m (3.75 m for down_the_line), which the exports keep. Measured on the committed demo bundle at address (golfer and club pixels from a MuJoCo segmentation render, first to last row over frame height): down_the_line 3.75 m (preset) 52%, 2.6 m 76%; face_on 3.5 m (preset) 60%, 2.8 m 74%. The owner asked on 2026-11-22 that the golfer fill the render; 70-80% leaves head and club clear of the frame edge.
sources.framing: How the render fills its area. The render is made at the view label's aspect (width over height), clamped to min_aspect..max_aspect and rounded to aspect_step so a drag-resize does not rebuild the renderer on every pixel; render_height_px is its height. A resize is debounced by resize_debounce_ms before the renderer is rebuilt. Past the clamp the picture keeps its shape and the label shows grey gutters.
sources.club_speed_plot: Club-head speed plot labels. impact_title shows the Shot card's club speed at the instant the face meets the ball (the card's fit of the samples before contact) and a marker of marker_color and marker_size_pt there, so the plot and the card never disagree; the plotted curve is a central difference that straddles the strike and reads lower (on the 2026-11-22 driver match 113.2 against 114.7 mph). peak_title is used when there is no card speed. Both templates take {speed} (mph) and {time} (s).

club_speed_plot.impact_title: Impact {speed:.1f} mph at t = {time:.3f} s (Shot card)
